title: Sums of primes, after Hardy and Littlewood 1923, Partitio Numerorum III, Theorems B to F proved without Hypothesis R
abstract: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof, with no hypothesis, of Theorems B, C, D, E and F of G. H. Hardy and J. E. Littlewood, Some problems of Partitio Numerorum III, Acta Math. 44, 1923. Hardy and Littlewood proved these theorems on their Hypothesis R, a form of the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions; here they are proved unconditionally, from Vinogradov's estimate for exponential sums over primes and the Siegel-Walfisz theorem, so the argument is not Hardy and Littlewood's own for Theorems B, D and E. Formalized: Theorem B, the asymptotic for the weighted count nu_r of n as an ordered sum of r primes, for every r at least 3 and n of the parity of r, with the singular series written as the paper's product over the odd primes dividing n, and nu_r of n is o of n^{r-1} for unlike parity; Theorem C, N_r of n is asymptotic to nu_r of n over log^r n; Theorem D, the ternary asymptotic with the constant C_3 and every large odd number a sum of three odd primes; Theorem E, the asymptotic for four odd primes, every large even number a sum of four odd primes, one of which may be assigned; and Theorem F, that an asymptotic of Conjecture A's shape for binary Goldbach can only carry the constant 2 C_2, together with a check that the printed formula 4.23 has a misprint. Theorem A of the paper is not formalized. Ternary Goldbach is Helfgott's theorem; binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent; the statements were written from the paper's page images by AI agents and are offered for human audit.
